cd /Users/dmitry/projects/worktrees/.plans/friction-queue && python3 - <<'PY'
p='spec.md'
s=open(p).read()
add='''
## 6a. Settled after the builder check (my calls, open to override)

1. **Apply on a rule entry** (a `restated` entry whose proposal carries a `Direction:`): Apply does what the
   morning step does today, `friction-ledger directions add` and the entry set `fixed --fix D-NNN`; it
   never goes to `coach-fix`. The card says "Apply adds the standing rule: <rule>".
2. **A guard-loosening card with no exact change written**: no Apply on it. The card says "no exact
   change written yet" and offers Reply (pre-filled hint: "write the exact change"), Later and Ignore.
   Apply only ever approves a change the user could read on the card.
3. **Approval is same-moment, not same-day.** The hook records the yes and runs `coach-fix enqueue`
   right away (detached, still the same date). If the enqueue is refused or fails, the card is re-filed
   with the reason on top; nothing waits for a next morning. A held safety fix (it goes back to
   `proposed`) is re-filed as a labelled card by the same card sync.
4. **The badge counts open cards in the friction deck.** A card answered with Reply closes; while its
   reply job runs, the deck shows nothing for it and the badge does not count it. The reply job runs
   under `coach-fix`'s existing stall watch (`COACH_JOB_MAX`, the dead-window check); a job that ends
   without a revision, crashes or stalls makes `coach-fix` re-file the card with "could not revise:
   <why>" and the user's words quoted.
5. **Reply is the app's own "type your own words" answer**: three options (Apply, Ignore, Later; for a
   secret Done, Later, Ignore) plus free text. Free text closes the card with `option: null` and the
   text, which the hook treats as Reply. The app's "tell" remark is not used. No app change is needed
   for answering; a change is made only if the card text or title needs it.
6. **A revision is a new ledger verb**, e.g. `friction-ledger revise F-NNN --proposal-file F --answer-file A`,
   that replaces the `## Proposal` section, appends the answer and the user's words to the entry's
   history, re-runs the safety check (so a revised proposal is re-labelled), and leaves the entry
   `offered` without clearing its fields; then the card is re-filed.
7. **No daily cap.** Every eligible entry is a card at once (today that is about eight: F-005, F-011,
   F-032, F-047, F-048, F-049, F-056, F-012). The "no flood" guard is the existing eligibility rules
   (a proposal exists; `repeat` entries need count ≥ 3 on ≥ 2 days; one card per entry), plus newest
   first in the deck. `coach-offer`'s 3-per-day limit and `coach-log`'s offered count go with the
   morning offer; `coach-log` keeps counting answers, landed, failed and cards.
'''
s=s.replace('\n## 7. Constraints', add+'\n## 7. Constraints')
open(p,'w').write(s)
PY
rg -n '^## ' spec.md
